experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting from Siglufjörður
experiences.description: Join a guided northern lights tour departing from Siglufjörður, venturing into the dark fjordside countryside away from light pollution. The remote location of Siglufjörður in northern Iceland makes it one of the best spots in the country to witness the aurora borealis dancing over the fjord and surrounding mountains.

experiences.name: Hofsós Infinity Hot Spring Pool
experiences.description: Visit the stunning Hofsós swimming pool, often called Iceland's most beautiful geothermal pool, perched on a cliff edge overlooking Skagafjörður fjord. A short scenic drive from Siglufjörður, this geothermally heated outdoor pool offers breathtaking panoramic views of the fjord and distant mountains, especially magical at sunset or under the northern lights.

experiences.name: Héðinsfjörður Abandoned Village Hike
experiences.description: Explore the hauntingly beautiful and completely uninhabited Héðinsfjörður fjord, accessible via a short tunnel from Siglufjörður. Hike through this remote valley to discover the ruins of an abandoned fishing village, dramatic waterfalls, and pristine Arctic nature. The fjord is surrounded by towering peaks and offers exceptional wildlife spotting including Arctic foxes and seabirds.

experiences.name: Herring Era Museum & Local Culture Experience
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Siglufjörður's rich cultural heritage at the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið), one of Iceland's finest regional museums. Explore restored warehouses and boats that tell the story of the great herring boom of the early 20th century. Pair the visit with a meal at a local restaurant sampling traditional Icelandic fish dishes and lamb soup.

experiences.name: Tröllaskagi Peninsula Whale Watching & Sea Safari
experiences.description: Embark on a sea safari from the nearby town of Dalvík or Ólafsfjörður, exploring the rich marine waters of Eyjafjörður — one of Iceland's longest fjords. These waters are home to humpback whales, minke whales, white-beaked dolphins, and harbour porpoises. The dramatic mountain scenery of the Tröllaskagi Peninsula provides a stunning backdrop for this unforgettable Arctic wildlife experience.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Héðinsfjörður Abandoned Village Hike
experiences.description: Explore the hauntingly beautiful and completely uninhabited Héðinsfjörður fjord, accessible via a short tunnel from Siglufjörður. Hike through this remote valley to discover the ruins of an abandoned fishing village, dramatic waterfalls, and pristine Arctic nature. The fjord is surrounded by towering peaks and offers exceptional wildlife spotting including Arctic foxes and seabirds.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the budget-friendly Flybus (Strætó) to Reykjavík BSÍ terminal (~45 min, ~3,000 ISK). Store luggage at BSÍ bus terminal locker while you explore. Walk around Reykjavík's old harbour and Tjörnin lake to stay awake and adjust to the time zone.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the long-distance Strætó bus (Route 57 or connecting service) toward Akureyri and then onward to Siglufjörður. The journey is long (~5–6 hours total) but scenic through the Icelandic winter landscape. Grab snacks and a thermos of coffee from a Bónus or Krónan supermarket near BSÍ before departure to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Siglufjörður and check into Hotel Siglunes on Lækjargata 10. Settle into your room, freshen up, and take a short evening stroll along the quiet harbour front. The small fishing town is beautifully lit in winter. Watch the sky for early northern lights activity — Siglufjörður's low light pollution makes it excellent for aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee at Keflavík Airport before departure (~800 ISK) or pack snacks from home.
meals.lunch: Packed snacks and sandwiches purchased at a Reykjavík Bónus supermarket (~600 ISK) eaten on the bus.
meals.dinner: Héðinsfjörður Bistro or Sigló Hótel restaurant for a warming bowl of lamb soup (kjötsúpa) — a budget-friendly Icelandic staple (~2,500–3,000 ISK). Alternatively, cook a simple meal in the hotel if kitchen facilities are available.

day_by_day.notes: Travel day — pace yourself. The Strætó bus is the most budget-friendly option (~5,000–6,000 ISK total from Reykjavík). Confirm bus schedules in advance at straeto.is as winter timetables are reduced. Dress in warm layers; January temperatures average around 0–5°C. Keep your camera accessible for potential aurora sightings on arrival.

day_by_day.morning: After a well-deserved rest, enjoy a slow morning. Walk along Siglufjörður's charming harbour and explore the town's colourful wooden houses dusted with snow. Visit the famous Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's best regional museums (~1,800 ISK entry) — which tells the story of the town's booming herring industry in the early 20th century.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the short but rewarding trail up the hillside above Siglufjörður for panoramic views of the fjord and surrounding snow-capped mountains. The trail starts near the edge of town and takes about 1.5–2 hours round trip. Dress in full winter gear and microspikes if icy. Return to town and warm up with a hot chocolate at a local café.
day_by_day.evening: Head out after dark (darkness falls by 16:00 in January) to a dark spot just outside town — the road toward the tunnel entrance or the harbour pier — for northern lights hunting. The Kp index forecast can be checked free at vedur.is. Bring a tripod for long-exposure photography.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats or yoghurt from supplies purchased at a local shop (~400 ISK).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch — rye bread (rúgbrauð) with smoked salmon or skyr from the local Samkaup or Krónan store (~700 ISK).
meals.dinner: Cook a simple pasta or rice dish in the hotel kitchen if available, or try the local grill/snack bar for a budget hot dog or burger (~1,200–1,800 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: January days are very short in Siglufjörður — expect only about 5 hours of usable daylight (roughly 11:00–16:00). Plan outdoor activities tightly within this window. Check aurora forecasts nightly at vedur.is or the Aurora Forecast app.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a local taxi through the Héðinsfjörður tunnel (opened 2010) to begin the Héðinsfjörður Abandoned Village Hike. This hauntingly beautiful uninhabited fjord was evacuated in 1951. Explore the ruins of the old farmsteads and imagine life in this remote, dramatic landscape surrounded by towering mountains and a frozen shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Héðinsfjörður at a leisurely pace. The fjord is completely uninhabited and utterly silent in winter — a truly otherworldly experience. Look for Arctic foxes, which are common in this area. Photograph the abandoned structures against the dramatic mountain backdrop. Return through the tunnel to Siglufjörður by mid-afternoon before darkness falls.
day_by_day.evening: Warm up back at Hotel Siglunes with a hot shower. Spend the evening relaxing and reviewing your aurora photos from previous nights. Head out again after 20:00 for another northern lights watch session from the harbour or hillside above town.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered eggs and toast at the hotel (~400 ISK).
meals.lunch: Packed thermos of soup and rye bread sandwiches eaten in Héðinsfjörður (~600 ISK). Bring extra snacks — there are no facilities in the fjord.
meals.dinner: Sigló Hótel bar menu or local grill — try the fish and chips or lamb burger (~2,000–2,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: The Héðinsfjörður hike is free of charge. Wear waterproof boots and full winter gear — the fjord can be windswept and icy. The tunnel toll is minimal (~500 ISK per car). If you don't have a rental car, arrange a local taxi or ask the hotel about shared transport options. Do not hike alone in winter without informing someone of your plans.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip east along Route 76 toward Hofsós, a tiny village on the Skagafjörður coast (~45 min drive). Visit the Icelandic Emigration Centre (Vesturfarasetrið) — a fascinating and affordable museum (~1,500 ISK) about Icelanders who emigrated to North America in the 19th century.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Hofsós Swimming Pool — one of Iceland's most scenic geothermal pools, perched dramatically above the fjord with stunning mountain views. Entry is very affordable (~1,000 ISK) and the pool is heated by geothermal energy. Soak in the hot tubs and enjoy the surreal winter landscape around you.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður along the scenic coastal road. Stop at a viewpoint along Route 76 to scan the sky for northern lights on the drive back. Enjoy a quiet evening at the hotel with a warm drink.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered cereal and skyr at the hotel (~400 ISK).
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the hotel or grab a sandwich from the Hofsós village store (~700 ISK).
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at the hotel — pasta with canned fish or a simple stew (~800 ISK from supermarket supplies).

day_by_day.notes: Hofsós is approximately 45 km from Siglufjörður via Route 76. Road conditions in January can be challenging — check road.is before departure. The Hofsós pool may have limited winter hours; confirm in advance. This is a great low-cost day combining culture and geothermal relaxation.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south to Varmahlíð in the Skagafjörður valley (~1 hour from Siglufjörður). Stop at Glaumbær Turf Farm Museum (Glaumbaer) — a beautifully preserved 18th-century turf farmhouse complex, one of Iceland's best examples of traditional architecture (~1,800 ISK entry). Walk through the low-ceilinged rooms and imagine winter life centuries ago.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Skagafjörður valley, known as Iceland's horse country. Even in winter, Icelandic horses roam the snowy fields — stop along the roadside to photograph and interact with them (they are famously friendly). Drive back toward Siglufjörður via the scenic Héðinsfjörður route for a different perspective.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights watch from the hillside above Siglufjörður. The valley orientation and low light pollution make this an excellent aurora viewing spot. Bring a flask of hot tea and a blanket for comfort during the wait.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — oats with honey and coffee (~400 ISK).
meals.lunch: Café Á Hlöðum at Glaumbær serves traditional Icelandic food including skyr cake and lamb soup (~1,500–2,000 ISK).
meals.dinner: Self-catered hearty stew using lamb or chicken from the supermarket (~900 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbær is approximately 60 km from Siglufjörður. Confirm winter opening hours before visiting — some Icelandic museums have reduced January hours. The Icelandic horse farms in Skagafjörður sometimes offer short winter rides; inquire locally if interested (budget ~5,000–8,000 ISK for a short ride).

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Spend the morning writing a travel journal, editing photos, or reading. Take a gentle walk along the Siglufjörður waterfront and explore any local shops or the small town centre.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Siglufjörður Folk Museum annexes — the town has multiple museum buildings including the Boat House and the Saltfish House, all included in the Herring Era Museum ticket if you kept your receipt (~1,800 ISK if purchasing fresh). Learn about the town's maritime heritage in depth.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local community event if available (check with the hotel for any winter concerts, bingo nights, or community gatherings — Icelanders are very welcoming to visitors). Otherwise, enjoy a cosy evening at the hotel bar or common area with fellow travellers.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered full Icelandic-style breakfast — skyr, rye bread, smoked salmon, eggs (~600 ISK).
meals.lunch: Local bakery or café in Siglufjörður — try a freshly baked kleina (twisted doughnut) and coffee (~800 ISK).
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner at the Sigló Hótel restaurant — the fish of the day is usually excellent and reasonably priced (~3,000–3,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: This is a planned rest day to recharge mid-trip. January weather in Siglufjörður can be harsh with storms — having a flexible indoor day built into the itinerary is practical. Use this time to plan the second half of the trip and check road conditions for upcoming excursions.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east along Route 1 (Ring Road) toward Akureyri, Iceland's second-largest city (~1.5 hours from Siglufjörður via the Ólafsfjörður tunnel). Arrive in Akureyri and explore the charming town centre. Visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on the hill — free entry — with beautiful stained glass windows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — free entry — the world's northernmost botanical garden, which is atmospheric and peaceful in winter snow. Browse the local shops along Hafnarstræti, Akureyri's main street. Stop at the Bónus supermarket to restock budget supplies for the coming days.
day_by_day.evening: Soak at Akureyri Swimming Pool (Sundlaug Akureyrar) — one of Iceland's best municipal pools with multiple hot tubs, steam room, and a waterslide (~1,000 ISK). Return to Siglufjörður in the evening, watching for northern lights on the mountain road.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before departure (~400 ISK).
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu-style hot dog from a snack bar in Akureyri (~500 ISK) or a soup of the day at a local café (~1,200 ISK).
meals.dinner: Strikið restaurant in Akureyri has a budget lunch/early dinner menu, or grab a pizza slice from a local takeaway (~1,500–2,000 ISK) before the drive back.

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is approximately 75 km from Siglufjörður. The drive through the Ólafsfjörður and Dalvík tunnels is straightforward but check road.is for winter conditions. Akureyri is a great place to stock up on supplies, visit an ATM, and enjoy a slightly more urban atmosphere mid-trip.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Dalvík (~30 min from Siglufjörður) and take the free Hrísey Island ferry (the ferry itself is free for foot passengers; small fee for cars). Explore Hrísey, Iceland's second-largest island, known as the 'Pearl of Eyjafjörður.' Walk the marked nature trails and look for ptarmigan and other winter birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the mainland and drive to the Árskógssandur area to visit the small but charming Dalvík Natural History Museum (Byggðasafn Dalvíkurbyggðar) — very affordable entry (~500 ISK) — which famously displays the skeleton of Iceland's tallest man ever recorded. Explore Dalvík's small harbour.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður via the scenic coastal road. Stop at a high point on the road for northern lights viewing — the stretch between Dalvík and Siglufjörður offers excellent dark sky conditions. Set up your camera for long-exposure aurora shots.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel (~400 ISK).
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos and sandwiches for the Hrísey island walk (~600 ISK). There is a small café on Hrísey but hours are limited in winter.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at hotel — oven-baked fish with potatoes and vegetables (~900 ISK from supermarket).

day_by_day.notes: The Hrísey ferry runs from Árskógssandur and takes about 15 minutes. Check the winter timetable at hrisey.net. The island is very quiet in January — you may have the trails almost entirely to yourself. Bring binoculars for birdwatching. The Dalvík area is also a good base for seeing the northern lights due to its position on the fjord.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south to the Mývatn region (~1.5 hours from Siglufjörður via Route 1 and Route 848). This volcanic wonderland is one of Iceland's most dramatic landscapes. Begin at the Námaskarð geothermal area (Hverir) — free entry — a surreal landscape of bubbling mud pools, steaming fumaroles, and vivid orange and yellow sulphur deposits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — a more affordable alternative to the Blue Lagoon (~5,500 ISK entry) with stunning views over the volcanic landscape. Soak in the milky blue geothermal waters surrounded by snow-covered lava fields. This is a quintessential Icelandic hot spring experience.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Siglufjörður, stopping at a dark roadside pullout for northern lights viewing. The Mývatn area and the roads north of Akureyri are excellent aurora locations. Alternatively, if weather is poor, return directly to the hotel for a warm evening in.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast at hotel before the drive (~400 ISK).
meals.lunch: Café at Mývatn Nature Baths serves soup and sandwiches (~1,500–2,000 ISK) or pack your own lunch to eat at Námaskarð.
meals.dinner: Gamli Bærinn restaurant near Mývatn for a budget lamb soup or fish dish (~2,000–2,500 ISK) before the drive back, or self-catered at hotel.

day_by_day.notes: Mývatn is approximately 100 km from Siglufjörður — a longer day trip but absolutely worth it. Start early to maximise the limited daylight hours. The Mývatn Nature Baths are significantly cheaper than the Blue Lagoon and equally beautiful. Road conditions on Route 1 in January can be icy — drive carefully and check road.is.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning walk along the Siglufjörður fjord shore, exploring the area north of town toward the end of the fjord. The landscape is dramatic in winter with snow-covered mountains reflected in the still water. Look for eider ducks and other seabirds along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive through the Héðinsfjörður tunnel for a second visit to the abandoned fjord, this time focusing on photography and quiet contemplation. The light in the early afternoon (around 13:00–15:00) can be beautiful and golden in January. Explore different parts of the fjord you may have missed on Day 3.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður and spend the evening at the hotel. If aurora activity is forecast (Kp 3+), head out to the harbour or hillside for viewing. This is also a good evening to try cooking a traditional Icelandic recipe — skyr pancakes or lamb stew — using local ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — eggs, rye bread, and coffee (~400 ISK).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten in Héðinsfjörður — thermos of soup and rye bread with cheese (~600 ISK).
meals.dinner: Self-catered Icelandic lamb stew (kjötsúpa) made with lamb, root vegetables, and herbs from the supermarket (~1,000 ISK for ingredients).

day_by_day.notes: This is a more relaxed day with familiar destinations revisited at a slower pace. Use the afternoon golden hour light for your best landscape photography of the trip. January 25th is approaching the end of the trip — begin thinking about packing and any souvenirs to purchase.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west along Route 76 to explore the Tröllaskagi peninsula coastline. Stop at Ólafsfjörður, a small fishing village similar to Siglufjörður, and walk around its harbour and town centre. Visit the small local swimming pool for a morning soak (~800 ISK).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving along the scenic coastal road (Route 82) toward Dalvík and then to the Vaðlaheiði viewpoint for panoramic views over Eyjafjörður. On a clear day, you can see all the way to Akureyri and the mountains beyond. Return to Siglufjörður via the tunnel route.
day_by_day.evening: Final major northern lights hunting evening — check the aurora forecast carefully and position yourself at the best available dark spot. The hillside above Siglufjörður or the road toward Héðinsfjörður are ideal. Stay out for 2–3 hours if conditions are favourable.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel (~400 ISK).
meals.lunch: Local bakery or café in Ólafsfjörður for fresh bread and soup (~1,000–1,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the Sigló Hótel or local restaurant — treat yourself to a traditional Icelandic fish dish or lamb (~2,500–3,000 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: This is your second-to-last full day in Siglufjörður — make the most of the local area. The Tröllaskagi peninsula is one of Iceland's most scenic regions and is often overlooked by tourists. Check if any local events are happening in Siglufjörður or Ólafsfjörður in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Siglufjörður. Take a slow farewell walk through the town, revisiting favourite spots — the harbour, the museum district, the hillside viewpoint. Purchase any last-minute souvenirs from local shops (Icelandic wool products, local jams, or dried fish are affordable and authentic).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Hotel Siglunes and begin the journey south toward Reykjavík. Take the Strætó bus or drive south via Route 1 through Akureyri. If driving, stop at Goðafoss waterfall (~45 min south of Akureyri on Route 1) — one of Iceland's most beautiful waterfalls, free to visit and stunning in winter ice.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Akureyri or continue south toward Reykjavík depending on your departure logistics. If staying overnight near the airport, book a budget guesthouse in Reykjavík or Keflavík (~8,000–12,000 ISK). Spend the evening packing and preparing for departure.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — use up remaining food supplies (~400 ISK).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch for the road or stop at a petrol station N1 or Orkan for a budget hot dog and coffee (~600 ISK).
meals.dinner: Budget dinner in Reykjavík — Hlöllabátar submarine sandwich shop or Bæjarins Beztu hot dog stand (~800–1,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: Goðafoss is approximately 50 km south of Akureyri and is free to visit. The waterfall is particularly dramatic in winter when partially frozen. The drive from Siglufjörður to Reykjavík is approximately 5–6 hours — start early. If using the Strætó bus, book tickets in advance at straeto.is as winter services can fill up.

day_by_day.morning: If time permits before departure, take a final morning visit to the Blue Lagoon (pre-book online, ~7,000–9,000 ISK for standard entry) which is conveniently located near Keflavík Airport — perfect for a last Icelandic hot spring experience before flying home. Alternatively, visit the free Reykjanes Peninsula lava fields and lighthouse for a budget-friendly farewell to Iceland's dramatic landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Keflavík International Airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and boarding. Browse the duty-free shop for last-minute Icelandic chocolate, Brennivín schnapps, or skyr products at airport prices.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with incredible memories of northern lights, geothermal hot springs, dramatic fjords, and the unique magic of the Tröllaskagi peninsula in winter.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the guesthouse or a café near the airport (~800–1,200 ISK).
meals.lunch: Airport café or bring packed snacks to avoid expensive airport food (~1,000 ISK if eating at airport).
meals.dinner: Onboard the flight or at your destination.

day_by_day.notes: If visiting the Blue Lagoon on departure day, book the earliest available slot (07:00 or 08:00) and pre-book online — walk-ins are not accepted. The Blue Lagoon is only 20 minutes from the airport. Leave enough buffer time to reach the airport comfortably. Confirm your flight details and check in online 24 hours before departure to save time.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage, then arrange a pre-booked rental car or airport transfer. Begin the scenic drive north toward Siglufjörður — approximately 4.5–5 hours via Route 1 and the Héðinsfjörður tunnel. Stop at a petrol station café near Akureyri for a break and fuel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the drive north through the dramatic Tröllaskagi Peninsula, passing through the single-lane Strákagil and Héðinsfjörður tunnels. Arrive at Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður by early afternoon. Check in, unpack, and rest after the overnight flight. Take a gentle stroll along the Siglufjörður harbour front to orient yourself with the town.
day_by_day.evening: Easy first evening — head to Hannes Boy restaurant (one of Siglufjörður's most beloved spots) for a warming bowl of lamb soup or fresh fish of the day. Return to the hotel early to rest and recover from travel fatigue. Keep an eye on the northern lights forecast app (Vedur.is) before bed.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee at the airport or a roadside petrol station café (Orkan or N1) en route north — budget around 1,500–2,000 ISK
meals.lunch: Stop at Bautinn restaurant in Akureyri during the drive north for a classic Icelandic meat soup or burger — mid-range, around 2,500–3,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy in Siglufjörður — cosy local favourite serving fresh fish and traditional Icelandic dishes — expect 4,000–6,000 ISK per person

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives early morning so the full day is essentially a travel day. Do not over-schedule. Prioritise rest. Download the Vedur.is app and the 112 Iceland safety app before leaving the airport. Rental car is strongly recommended for this itinerary — book in advance. Roads in January can be icy; request a 4WD vehicle.

day_by_day.morning: After a proper night's sleep, enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Then visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's finest regional museums, spread across three restored warehouses on the harbour. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the fascinating history of Siglufjörður's herring boom era of the early 20th century, complete with reconstructed salting stations and period artefacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the compact town centre and explore the colourful wooden houses lining the fjord. Visit the local swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) — a small but authentic Icelandic community pool with a hot pot, perfect for warming up and meeting locals. Spend 1–1.5 hours soaking and relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting from Siglufjörður — join a guided northern lights tour departing from the town. The guide will drive to optimal dark-sky locations along the fjordside, away from any light pollution, to maximise aurora viewing chances. Tours typically run 2–3 hours depending on conditions.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast included or available — enjoy skyr, rye bread, smoked salmon and coffee
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka café in Siglufjörður — a charming local café serving homemade soups, sandwiches and cakes — around 2,000–3,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Sigló Hótel restaurant (open to non-guests) for a slightly elevated dinner of pan-fried Arctic char or lamb fillet — 5,000–7,500 ISK per person

day_by_day.notes: The Herring Era Museum may have reduced winter hours — confirm opening times in advance (typically 10:00–18:00 in summer, shorter in winter). Northern lights tours from Siglufjörður are weather-dependent; the guide will cancel or reschedule if cloud cover is total. January offers long dark nights (roughly 18–19 hours of darkness) which is ideal for aurora hunting. KP index of 3+ gives good viewing chances.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along the Tröllaskagi Peninsula (Route 76) to the village of Hofsós — approximately 45 minutes from Siglufjörður. Visit the spectacular Hofsós Infinity Hot Spring Pool, perched dramatically on a cliff edge above Skagafjörður with panoramic fjord views. Arrive early (pool opens around 09:00) to enjoy it before crowds. Spend 1.5–2 hours soaking in the geothermal waters with views of snow-dusted mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming village of Hofsós itself — visit the Icelandic Emigration Centre (Vesturfarasetrið), which tells the story of 19th-century Icelandic emigrants to North America. Browse the small gift shop. Drive back toward Siglufjörður via the scenic coastal road, stopping at viewpoints over Skagafjörður.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður by late afternoon. Spend the evening at the hotel relaxing. If the northern lights forecast is strong (KP 3+), venture out independently to the harbour or drive a short distance out of town for aurora viewing — the fjord setting provides a stunning reflection backdrop.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pick up supplies from Krónan supermarket in Siglufjörður for a self-catered morning
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch from the supermarket to eat near Hofsós — rye bread, smoked lamb (hangikjöt), cheese and fruit — budget around 1,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy restaurant again or try cooking in if your hotel room has kitchen facilities — pick up fresh fish from the local fish market or supermarket — budget 2,000–3,000 ISK self-catered

day_by_day.notes: Hofsós pool is one of Iceland's most photogenic — bring a waterproof camera or phone case. Water temperature is typically 36–38°C. The drive between Siglufjörður and Hofsós is scenic but can be icy in January — drive carefully and check road conditions on road.is before departing. The Icelandic Emigration Centre may have limited winter hours.

day_by_day.morning: Héðinsfjörður Abandoned Village Hike — drive through the Héðinsfjörður tunnel (free, single-lane) and park at the tunnel exit on the fjord side. Explore the hauntingly beautiful and completely uninhabited Héðinsfjörður fjord on foot. The flat valley floor makes for an accessible winter walk. Visit the ruins of the abandoned farmsteads, old church foundations and stone walls — a deeply atmospheric experience in the winter silence.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Héðinsfjörður or return through the tunnel and drive to nearby Ólafsfjörður (15 minutes from Siglufjörður via tunnel). Walk around this small fishing village, visit the local swimming pool for a warm-up soak, and browse the small shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður for dinner. Spend the evening at the hotel with a good book or planning the rest of the trip. Check northern lights forecast — if conditions are favourable, take a short drive out of town after dinner for aurora hunting.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos of hot coffee and sandwiches for the Héðinsfjörður hike — essential for warmth in January
meals.dinner: Sigló Hótel restaurant or Hannes Boy — try the traditional Icelandic lamb stew (kjötsúpa) — 4,000–6,000 ISK per person

day_by_day.notes: The Héðinsfjörður hike is relatively flat and accessible but dress in full winter layers — waterproof jacket, thermal base layers, wool mid-layer, waterproof boots with grip, hat and gloves. Daylight in January is very limited (roughly 5–6 hours, approximately 11:00–16:00) so start the hike no later than 11:00. The fjord is completely uninhabited and there is no mobile signal — inform someone of your plans. The tunnel is single-lane with passing places.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south to Dalvík (approximately 1 hour from Siglufjörður via Route 82 and the Vaðlaheiðargöng tunnel). Embark on the Tröllaskagi Peninsula Whale Watching & Sea Safari — a guided boat tour from Dalvík exploring the rich marine waters of Eyjafjörður, one of Iceland's longest fjords. Arctic Whale Tours operates year-round from Dalvík and frequently spots humpback whales, minke whales and white-beaked dolphins even in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Dalvík after the tour (typically 2–3 hours). Explore Dalvík briefly — visit the quirky Byggðasafnið Hvoll folk museum, which houses a fascinating exhibit on the 'Giant of Dalvík', an Icelander who grew to 2.34 metres tall. Drive back toward Siglufjörður, stopping in Ólafsfjörður for a coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting from Siglufjörður — second guided tour attempt (or independent viewing if the first tour was successful). The long January nights provide ample opportunity. Alternatively, relax at the hotel and enjoy a quiet evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eat well before the boat tour
meals.lunch: Gísli, Eiríkur, Helgi restaurant in Dalvík — a beloved local spot known for excellent fish and chips and fresh seafood — 2,500–4,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy or self-catered at the hotel — pick up groceries from Krónan in Siglufjörður

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching in January is weather and sea-condition dependent — Arctic Whale Tours has a high success rate but tours can be cancelled in rough seas. Book in advance and confirm the morning of. Dress in extreme warmth for the boat — the wind chill on the water is severe. The company provides overalls but bring your own thermal layers underneath. The Vaðlaheiðargöng tunnel toll is approximately 1,500 ISK each way — have a card ready.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — sleep in and enjoy a slow hotel breakfast. Spend the morning exploring Siglufjörður's harbour area at leisure. Visit the small local art gallery or browse the handful of boutique shops in town. Pick up any local souvenirs — Icelandic wool products (lopapeysa sweaters) are excellent value here compared to Reykjavík.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the scenic Route 76 south along the western coast of the Tröllaskagi Peninsula toward Sauðárkrókur (approximately 1.5 hours). Visit the Glaumbær turf farm museum — one of Iceland's best-preserved historic turf farmsteads, offering a vivid glimpse into traditional Icelandic rural life. The farm dates to the 18th century and is a National Museum of Iceland site.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður via the same route. Enjoy dinner at the hotel restaurant or Hannes Boy. Spend the evening monitoring the northern lights forecast — January 21 falls during a period of long darkness, ideal for aurora activity.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — take your time
meals.lunch: Kaffi Krókur in Sauðárkrókur — a cosy café serving homemade soups and baked goods — 2,000–3,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Sigló Hótel restaurant — treat yourself to a slightly more indulgent dinner of pan-seared lamb with root vegetables — 5,500–8,000 ISK per person

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbær turf farm has limited winter opening hours — check in advance (often open 10:00–16:00 in winter). The drive to Sauðárkrókur via Route 76 is scenic but can be challenging in icy conditions — check road.is. This is a good day to do laundry at the hotel if needed. Sauðárkrókur is the largest town in the Skagafjörður region and has a well-stocked supermarket (Krónan) if you need supplies.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east from Siglufjörður through the tunnels to Akureyri — Iceland's second city, approximately 1 hour away. Spend the morning exploring Akureyri: visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church (free entry) perched dramatically above the town, and stroll the pedestrianised Hafnarstræti shopping street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Art Museum (Listasafnið á Akureyri) or the Akureyri Museum (Minjasafnið á Akureyri) for cultural depth. Then head to the Akureyri geothermal swimming pool (Sundlaug Akureyrar) — one of the best municipal pools in Iceland, with multiple hot pots, a steam room and a 50-metre outdoor pool. Spend 1.5–2 hours here.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Akureyri before driving back to Siglufjörður. Akureyri has the best restaurant selection in northern Iceland. Return to the hotel by 21:00 and check the northern lights forecast for late-night viewing.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing
meals.lunch: Bautinn restaurant in Akureyri — a classic, reliable Icelandic restaurant serving generous portions of fish, lamb and burgers — 2,500–4,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Rub23 in Akureyri — excellent sushi and Icelandic fusion cuisine in a stylish setting — 5,000–8,000 ISK per person; or Strikið for panoramic fjord views and Icelandic lamb

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is a worthwhile day trip from Siglufjörður and offers the most urban experience of the trip. The town has a warm, festive atmosphere even in January. The drive back to Siglufjörður after dinner will be in complete darkness — drive carefully on icy roads and watch for the northern lights en route. Akureyri has a good selection of shops if you need any gear or supplies.

day_by_day.morning: Full day excursion to the Mývatn region — drive from Siglufjörður to Lake Mývatn (approximately 1.5–2 hours via Akureyri and Route 1 east). Begin at the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — a stunning geothermal lagoon set in a volcanic landscape, often called the 'Blue Lagoon of the North' but far less crowded. Arrive when it opens (typically 09:00) and soak for 1.5–2 hours in the silica-rich, milky-blue waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the extraordinary volcanic landscape around Lake Mývatn: visit the Dimmuborgir lava formations (otherworldly lava pillars and arches), the Skútustaðagígar pseudocraters (a UNESCO-nominated landscape), and the Hverfjall tephra crater rim walk if conditions allow. The area is geologically unique and visually dramatic even under winter skies.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Siglufjörður (1.5–2 hours). Stop at a petrol station in Akureyri for a hot drink and snack. Return to the hotel and rest. If the northern lights forecast is strong, set an alarm for midnight and venture out.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eat well before the long day
meals.lunch: Vogafjós Farm Restaurant at Lake Mývatn — a unique farm-to-table experience where you can watch cows being milked through a glass wall while eating fresh skyr, geothermal rye bread and smoked trout — 3,000–5,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-catered at the hotel or a simple meal at Hannes Boy upon return — 3,500–5,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Mývatn Nature Baths are significantly less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and offer a more authentic experience — book online in advance (approximately 5,500–6,500 ISK per person). The volcanic landscape around Mývatn is extraordinary but paths can be icy in January — wear crampons or ice grips (Broddar) which can be purchased at any Icelandic hardware or outdoor shop. This is a long day — approximately 3–4 hours of driving total. Start early.

day_by_day.morning: Slower morning — enjoy hotel breakfast and a leisurely start. Take a winter walk along the Siglufjörður fjord shore, watching for seabirds and enjoying the dramatic mountain scenery. The town is beautifully quiet in January and the snow-covered peaks reflecting in the fjord are stunning in the limited morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Hofsós Infinity Hot Spring Pool for a second visit — this time in the afternoon light (around 13:00–15:00) when the low winter sun creates golden-hour conditions over Skagafjörður. The pool is magical in these conditions. Spend 1.5 hours soaking and photographing the view.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting from Siglufjörður — third opportunity with the guided tour or independent viewing. By now you will know the best local spots. The fjord's dark skies and reflective water surface make for spectacular aurora photography. Bring a tripod if you have one.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic or stop at the small café in Hofsós village
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy restaurant — try the pan-fried cod with butter sauce and Icelandic potatoes — 4,500–6,500 ISK per person

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberately lighter day to allow rest and flexibility. If the northern lights were missed on previous nights, tonight is another excellent opportunity — January 24 is well into the dark season. The Hofsós pool in afternoon golden light is one of the most photographic experiences in Iceland — bring your best camera. Check road.is before driving to Hofsós.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Akureyri and continue east on Route 1 to the Goðafoss waterfall — approximately 1.5 hours from Siglufjörður. Goðafoss ('Waterfall of the Gods') is one of Iceland's most spectacular waterfalls, with a wide horseshoe shape and powerful flow. In winter, the surrounding rocks are often draped in ice formations. Walk the short paths on both sides of the river for different perspectives.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Húsavík — Iceland's whale watching capital, approximately 1 hour from Goðafoss. Visit the Húsavík Whale Museum (Hvalasafnið) — an excellent natural history museum with full whale skeletons and interactive exhibits. Walk the charming harbour front and browse the small town.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Siglufjörður (approximately 2 hours via Akureyri). Enjoy a quiet dinner at the hotel or Hannes Boy. Rest well.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing
meals.lunch: Gamli Baukur restaurant in Húsavík — a classic harbourside restaurant in a historic wooden building, serving excellent fish soup and fresh catch — 3,000–4,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Sigló Hótel restaurant or self-catered — 3,000–6,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Goðafoss is accessible year-round and the paths are generally manageable in winter with proper footwear — ice grips recommended. The waterfall is particularly dramatic in winter with ice formations. Húsavík is famous for whale watching but winter tours are limited — the Whale Museum is the best winter option. This is another long driving day — approximately 4 hours total — so start by 09:00. Check road.is for Route 1 conditions east of Akureyri.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated photography and nature morning in and around Siglufjörður. The limited winter daylight (approximately 11:00–16:00) means the golden hour lasts most of the day. Walk to the end of the harbour pier for panoramic fjord views, then drive a short distance out of town on Route 76 for elevated viewpoints over the fjord and town. The snow-covered mountains and colourful houses make for exceptional photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Siglufjörður swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) for a relaxing soak in the hot pots — a quintessential Icelandic experience. Chat with locals, who are typically very welcoming to visitors. Spend 1–1.5 hours here. Then explore any remaining parts of the Herring Era Museum you may have missed on Day 2.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights Hunting from Siglufjörður guided tour — or independent viewing from the best spots you have identified during the trip. This is one of the last opportunities for a guided tour. Celebrate any aurora sightings with a glass of Brennivín (Icelandic schnapps) back at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka — homemade soup and fresh bread — 2,000–3,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy — final dinner here, try anything you haven't yet — 4,500–6,500 ISK per person

day_by_day.notes: This is a flexible day designed to catch up on anything missed or revisit favourites. If the weather has been consistently poor for northern lights, tonight may be the best remaining chance — January 26 still offers very long dark nights. The Siglufjörður swimming pool is a wonderful place to meet locals and experience everyday Icelandic life. Entry is typically 1,000–1,200 ISK.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — begin with a farewell walk through Siglufjörður, taking in the town one last time. Visit any shops for last-minute souvenirs — Icelandic wool products, local jams, dried fish (harðfiskur) or Brennivín make excellent gifts. Pack bags and prepare for checkout the following morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Akureyri for a final afternoon in Iceland's north. Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — the world's northernmost botanical garden, which is peaceful and atmospheric even in winter. Then browse the shops on Hafnarstræti for any remaining souvenirs or gifts. Visit the Akureyri Geothermal Pool one more time if desired.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Akureyri before driving back to Siglufjörður for the last night. Alternatively, if the flight departure logistics allow, consider staying in Akureyri for the final night to reduce driving on departure day — check with Hotel Siglunes about checkout flexibility.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — final morning at Siglunes
meals.lunch: Bláa Kannan café in Akureyri — a charming café in a historic blue building, serving excellent coffee, cakes and light lunches — 2,000–3,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Strikið restaurant in Akureyri — rooftop views over Eyjafjörður, excellent Icelandic lamb and fish dishes — 5,500–8,500 ISK per person; a fitting farewell dinner

day_by_day.notes: If your return flight departs from Keflavík (as most international flights do), plan the departure day drive carefully — it is approximately 5–6 hours from Siglufjörður to Keflavík. Consider whether it makes more sense to drive to Akureyri or Reykjavík on Day 12 evening to reduce Day 13 travel stress. Check your return flight time carefully and work backwards. Road conditions in January can add significant time to journeys.

day_by_day.morning: Checkout from Hotel Siglunes. Begin the drive south toward Keflavík International Airport — approximately 5–6 hours depending on road conditions and stops. Take Route 1 south via Akureyri, then continue south through the highland interior (if open) or via the Ring Road through Borgarnes. Stop at Hraunfossar and Barnafoss waterfalls near Reykholt if time allows — a beautiful final nature stop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in the Reykjavík/Keflavík area by early afternoon. If time permits before the flight, stop at the Reykjanes Peninsula for a final geothermal experience — the Reykjanes area has numerous free hot spring areas and dramatic volcanic landscapes near the airport. Return the rental car at Keflavík Airport with sufficient time (allow 1.5–2 hours before departure for car return, shuttle and check-in).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland from Keflavík International Airport. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days in the land of fire and ice — northern lights, geothermal pools, dramatic fjords and the warmth of Icelandic hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or grab supplies from Krónan supermarket for the road
meals.lunch: Stop at a petrol station restaurant (N1 or Orkan) en route south — reliable, warm and budget-friendly — 1,500–2,500 ISK; or pack sandwiches from the supermarket
meals.dinner: Airport meal at Keflavík — Fiskmarkaðurinn or Isavia airport restaurants — 3,500–5,500 ISK; or eat in Reykjavík if time allows before heading to the airport

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — start no later than 08:00 to allow comfortable time for the journey south, any stops, car return and airport procedures. Check road.is the night before for Route 1 conditions. January can bring significant snowfall and ice on the Ring Road — drive to conditions and allow extra time. Fill the rental car with petrol before returning it (petrol stations at Keflavík airport are expensive). Keep warm layers accessible in the car rather than packed in the boot.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting from Siglufjörður
experiences.description: Join a guided northern lights tour departing from Siglufjörður, venturing into the dark fjordside countryside away from light pollution. The remote location of Siglufjörður in northern Iceland makes it one of the best spots in the country to witness the aurora borealis dancing over the fjord and surrounding mountains.

experiences.name: Hofsós Infinity Hot Spring Pool
experiences.description: Visit the stunning Hofsós swimming pool, often called Iceland's most beautiful geothermal pool, perched on a cliff edge overlooking Skagafjörður fjord. A short scenic drive from Siglufjörður, this geothermally heated outdoor pool offers breathtaking panoramic views of the fjord and distant mountains, especially magical at sunset or under the northern lights.

experiences.name: Héðinsfjörður Abandoned Village Hike
experiences.description: Explore the hauntingly beautiful and completely uninhabited Héðinsfjörður fjord, accessible via a short tunnel from Siglufjörður. Hike through this remote valley to discover the ruins of an abandoned fishing village, dramatic waterfalls, and pristine Arctic nature. The fjord is surrounded by towering peaks and offers exceptional wildlife spotting including Arctic foxes and seabirds.

experiences.name: Herring Era Museum & Local Culture Experience
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Siglufjörður's rich cultural heritage at the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið), one of Iceland's finest regional museums. Explore restored warehouses and boats that tell the story of the great herring boom of the early 20th century. Pair the visit with a meal at a local restaurant sampling traditional Icelandic fish dishes and lamb soup.

experiences.name: Tröllaskagi Peninsula Whale Watching & Sea Safari
experiences.description: Embark on a sea safari from the nearby town of Dalvík or Ólafsfjörður, exploring the rich marine waters of Eyjafjörður — one of Iceland's longest fjords. These waters are home to humpback whales, minke whales, white-beaked dolphins, and harbour porpoises. The dramatic mountain scenery of the Tröllaskagi Peninsula provides a stunning backdrop for this unforgettable Arctic wildlife experience.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage, then meet your pre-arranged private luxury transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar). Begin the scenic 5–6 hour drive north toward Siglufjörður, stopping briefly at a roadside café near Borgarnes for a warm-up break.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the drive through the dramatic Tröllaskagi Peninsula, passing through the Héðinsfjörður and Ólafsfjörður tunnels. Arrive at Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður by early afternoon. Check in, settle into your room, and enjoy a welcome drink at the hotel. Take a gentle, leisurely stroll along the harbour front to orient yourself with the charming fishing town.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recover from travel. Head to dinner at Hannes Boy restaurant in Siglufjörður, the town's most celebrated dining spot known for fresh Arctic char, lamb, and locally sourced ingredients. Afterward, step outside to scan the skies for a first glimpse of the northern lights — January darkness arrives early and Siglufjörður's fjord location offers excellent aurora viewing right from town.

meals.breakfast: Light snack or coffee at a roadside stop near Borgarnes during the transfer drive
meals.lunch: Packed premium lunch box arranged by your transfer service, enjoyed en route
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy, Siglufjörður — Arctic char with herb butter, slow-roasted Icelandic lamb, and skyr-based dessert; pair with Icelandic craft beer or a curated wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day is intentionally relaxed. Jet lag and a long transfer mean rest is a priority. Confirm northern lights alert notifications via the Icelandic Met Office app (vedur.is) — aurora forecast checking becomes a nightly ritual throughout the trip. Hotel Siglunes staff can advise on real-time sky conditions.

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely hotel breakfast, embark on the Héðinsfjörður Abandoned Village Hike. Drive the short distance to the tunnel entrance and enter the hauntingly beautiful, completely uninhabited Héðinsfjörður fjord. A knowledgeable local guide leads you through the snow-dusted landscape past the ruins of the old farmstead Héðinsstaðir, sharing stories of the families who once lived here. The fjord's silence and dramatic mountain walls make this an otherworldly winter experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siglufjörður and warm up with lunch. Spend the afternoon at the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið), one of Iceland's finest regional museums. Explore three beautifully restored buildings documenting the town's explosive herring boom of the early 20th century, complete with original boats, equipment, and evocative period reconstructions. A private guided tour can be arranged for a more immersive experience.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting from Siglufjörður — join a guided aurora tour departing from the hotel. Your expert guide drives you into the dark fjordside countryside away from any light pollution, positioning the group at prime viewing spots along the fjord shores and mountain foothills. Hot chocolate and warm blankets provided. Photography assistance available for capturing the aurora.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — skyr with berries, smoked salmon, rye bread, eggs, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka, Siglufjörður — cosy café with homemade soups, open-faced sandwiches, and fresh pastries
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy or hotel dining — pan-seared cod with langoustine bisque, followed by Icelandic cheese board and cloudberry compote

day_by_day.notes: Dress in thermal base layers, mid-layer fleece, and a waterproof outer shell for the hike — temperatures will be well below 5°C in the fjord. The northern lights tour typically runs 21:00–00:00; aurora activity depends on geomagnetic conditions (KP index 2+ recommended). January offers up to 18 hours of darkness, maximising aurora opportunity.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along the Tröllaskagi Peninsula to the village of Hofsós (approximately 45 minutes). Visit the stunning Hofsós Infinity Hot Spring Pool, perched dramatically on a cliff edge above Skagafjörður with panoramic views of the fjord and distant mountains. In winter, the contrast of steaming geothermal water against the cold air and potential snow-capped peaks is extraordinary. Spend a luxurious 90 minutes soaking in the infinity pool and hot pots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming village of Hofsós, including the Icelandic Emigration Centre, which documents the thousands of Icelanders who emigrated to North America in the 19th century. Browse the small local craft shop. Return to Siglufjörður via the scenic coastal road, stopping at a viewpoint above the fjord for photography.
day_by_day.evening: Private in-hotel dining experience — arrange with Hotel Siglunes for a curated tasting menu served in the hotel's intimate dining space. Alternatively, enjoy a quiet evening at the hotel bar with Icelandic spirits (Brennivín, Reyka vodka) before an early night to rest for tomorrow's adventures.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — warm oatmeal porridge with Icelandic honey, fresh fruit, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch from the hotel, enjoyed with views of Skagafjörður near Hofsós
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes private dining — chef's tasting menu featuring seasonal Icelandic ingredients; request advance booking

day_by_day.notes: Hofsós pool is open year-round but hours may be limited in winter — confirm opening times in advance (typically 10:00–21:00). Bring a swimsuit, towel (or rent on-site), and a warm robe for the walk between changing rooms and the pool. The drive between Siglufjörður and Hofsós is scenic but can be icy — drive carefully or arrange a local driver.

day_by_day.morning: Tröllaskagi Peninsula Whale Watching & Sea Safari — depart early for the nearby town of Dalvík or Ólafsfjörður (approximately 30–45 minutes from Siglufjörður through the tunnel). Board a premium sea safari vessel equipped with heated cabins and expert marine guides. The waters of Eyjafjörður are among Iceland's most productive for humpback whales, white-beaked dolphins, and harbour porpoises even in winter. Binoculars and warm overalls provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to port and drive back toward Siglufjörður. Stop in Ólafsfjörður for a warm lunch. Spend the afternoon back at the hotel in relaxation — use this time for a spa treatment if available, or simply read by the window watching the fjord light change through the short winter afternoon (sunset around 15:30–16:00 in January).
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights hunting — second dedicated aurora excursion. Tonight, your guide takes you to a different location: a high mountain road above the fjord (weather and road conditions permitting) for an elevated, 360-degree aurora viewing experience. The guide provides a brief astronomy and aurora science talk while you wait for the lights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — smoked lamb (hangikjöt), rye bread, soft-boiled eggs, and Icelandic dairy
meals.lunch: Ólafsfjarðarkaffi or local restaurant in Ólafsfjörður — fish soup, fresh bread, and Icelandic butter
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy, Siglufjörður — slow-braised reindeer with root vegetable purée and juniper jus, followed by warm skyr cake

day_by_day.notes: Sea safari tours in winter require advance booking — confirm with operators such as Arctic Sea Tours or Whale Watching Dalvík. Dress in maximum warmth layers; the sea feels significantly colder than land. Motion sickness medication recommended if sensitive. Whale sightings are not guaranteed but success rates in Eyjafjörður are high year-round.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated photography morning — hire a local photography guide to accompany you around Siglufjörður's most photogenic winter scenes: the colourful harbour with fishing boats, the snow-laden rooftops of the old town, the dramatic mountain backdrop, and the frozen waterfalls visible on the fjord walls. The blue hour light in January (approximately 10:00–12:00) creates extraordinary pastel tones.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Herring Era Museum again for any exhibits missed on Day 2, or explore the town's small art galleries and craft boutiques. Stop at the local swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) for a relaxing geothermal soak — a beloved local tradition. The pool includes hot pots and a steam room.
day_by_day.evening: Self-guided aurora watching from the hotel or harbour area. January in Siglufjörður offers some of Iceland's darkest skies due to the deep fjord geography. Set up a tripod on the harbour pier for long-exposure aurora photography. Hotel staff can alert you if the lights appear strongly.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Icelandic pancakes (pönnukökur) with whipped cream and jam, fresh juice, and coffee
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka — homemade lamb soup, sourdough bread, and a slice of traditional Icelandic cake
meals.dinner: Private chef experience — arrange through the hotel for a local chef to prepare a traditional Icelandic feast in the hotel dining room: salt cod, smoked lamb, and skyr dessert

day_by_day.notes: The photography guide can be arranged through the hotel or local tourism contacts — expect to pay 25,000–40,000 ISK for a half-day session. The local swimming pool is an authentic Icelandic experience distinct from tourist-oriented hot springs — bring your own swimsuit and follow pool etiquette (shower without swimsuit before entering).

day_by_day.morning: Day excursion to Akureyri — Iceland's second city, approximately 1 hour from Siglufjörður via the Tröllaskagi tunnels. Arrange a private driver for comfort. Explore Akureyri's charming town centre: visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched above the city, browse the Akureyri Art Museum, and walk the pedestrianised Hafnarstræti shopping street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — the world's northernmost botanical garden, beautiful even in winter with its snow-covered structures. Explore the Akureyri Museum for regional history. Enjoy a premium lunch at one of Akureyri's finest restaurants before the return drive.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður by late afternoon. Enjoy a quiet evening at the hotel — order room service or dine at the hotel restaurant. Check aurora forecasts and, if conditions are favourable (KP index 3+), venture out for a spontaneous aurora viewing session along the harbour.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread including smoked salmon, cream cheese, rye crispbread, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Rub23 Restaurant, Akureyri — acclaimed for its sushi and Icelandic fusion cuisine; try the Arctic char sashimi and langoustine tempura
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes dining or room service — Icelandic lamb stew with root vegetables and fresh bread

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is a worthwhile contrast to the remote intimacy of Siglufjörður — it offers more shopping, cultural institutions, and dining variety. The drive through the Tröllaskagi tunnels is straightforward but confirm road conditions (road.is) before departure. A private driver costs approximately 30,000–50,000 ISK for the day but is worth the comfort and safety on potentially icy roads.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day snowmobile or snowcat adventure — arrange through a local operator for a guided snowmobile tour into the mountains above Siglufjörður. The Tröllaskagi highlands receive heavy snowfall and offer dramatic terrain. Ride through pristine snowfields with panoramic views of multiple fjords. No prior experience necessary; full safety briefing and equipment provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the snowmobile tour or, if preferred, transition to a guided snowshoeing experience through the quieter mountain valleys. The afternoon light (golden hour begins around 13:30 in January) creates spectacular photography conditions on the snow-covered slopes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a well-earned hot shower and relaxation. Treat yourself to a premium in-room spa experience — arrange a massage therapist to visit the hotel (bookable through concierge). Dine at Hannes Boy for a celebrious mid-trip dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — high-energy options: porridge, eggs, smoked meats, and strong coffee to fuel the day
meals.lunch: Packed hot thermos lunch provided by the snowmobile tour operator — soup, sandwiches, and hot chocolate in the mountains
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy — chef's special tasting menu; request the full experience with wine pairing (Icelandic and international selections)

day_by_day.notes: Snowmobile tours are weather and snow-condition dependent — have a backup plan (museum visit or spa day) if conditions are unsuitable. Minimum age and weight restrictions apply; confirm with operator. Dress in full thermal layers; the operator provides outer snowsuits, helmets, and gloves. Cost approximately 25,000–45,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.morning: Return visit to Hofsós Infinity Hot Spring Pool for a longer, more indulgent soak — this time arriving at opening time to enjoy the pool in near-solitude before day visitors arrive. Spend 2 hours in the geothermal waters, alternating between the infinity pool and the smaller hot pots, watching the winter light slowly illuminate the fjord.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the scenic Skagafjörður coastal road south from Hofsós, stopping at the historic Glaumbær turf farm museum (open limited hours in winter — confirm in advance). This beautifully preserved 18th-century turf farmhouse complex offers a fascinating window into traditional Icelandic rural life. Return to Siglufjörður via the inland route for a different perspective on the landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting — third dedicated aurora excursion with your guide. Tonight's focus: a remote fjordside location with a clear northern horizon, ideal for photographing the aurora reflected in the still waters of the fjord. Your guide brings a portable telescope for stargazing between aurora displays.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — lighter option: skyr parfait with granola, fresh berries, and herbal tea
meals.lunch: Café at Glaumbær or packed lunch from hotel, enjoyed in the car with fjord views
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — request a special dinner featuring traditional Icelandic dishes: hákarl (fermented shark, for the adventurous), smoked lamb, and kleinur (Icelandic doughnuts) for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbær turf farm has limited winter opening hours — call ahead to confirm (tel: +354 453 6173). The Skagafjörður coastal drive is one of Iceland's most scenic but can be icy; drive slowly and check road conditions. The aurora excursion tonight is the most remote of the trip — dress in maximum warmth layers and bring hand warmers.

day_by_day.morning: Guided ice climbing or glacier walk experience — arrange through a specialist operator for a half-day introduction to ice climbing on one of the frozen waterfalls in the mountains above Siglufjörður or in the broader Tröllaskagi region. Expert guides provide all equipment (crampons, ice axes, harnesses) and instruction. A truly unique and exhilarating winter activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Recovery and relaxation afternoon at the hotel. Enjoy the hotel's common areas, read, journal, or simply watch the dramatic winter light play across the fjord from your room window. Optional: visit the local swimming pool for a restorative geothermal soak.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style premium dinner at Hannes Boy (or hotel dining) — order the most indulgent items on the menu: whole roasted Arctic char, langoustine bisque, and a bottle of fine Champagne or white Burgundy to celebrate the journey so far.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread; fuel up well before the physical morning activity
meals.lunch: Hot soup and sandwiches at a local café in Siglufjörður post-activity
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy — premium tasting menu with Champagne or wine pairing; reserve in advance

day_by_day.notes: Ice climbing requires a reasonable level of physical fitness but no prior experience. The guide will assess conditions and choose the most suitable frozen waterfall. Activity typically runs 09:00–13:00. Cost approximately 20,000–35,000 ISK per person. If ice climbing is unavailable due to conditions, substitute with a guided winter hiking tour in the Héðinsfjörður area.

day_by_day.morning: Cultural immersion morning — arrange a private cooking class with a local Icelandic chef, learning to prepare traditional dishes: skyr-marinated lamb, rye bread baked in geothermal ground (hverabrauð), and Icelandic fish cakes. The class takes place in a local kitchen and includes a tasting of everything prepared.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Siglufjörður's lesser-known corners — visit the town's small but charming folk museum, browse the harbour fish market (if operating), and walk the full length of the harbour promenade. Stop at the local bakery for fresh kleinur and a coffee. Spend time at the hotel's lounge area reviewing photos and memories from the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Aurora hunting — spontaneous excursion based on forecast. If KP index is favourable, drive with your guide to a new location: the mountain road above the Héðinsfjörður tunnel entrance, offering a dramatic elevated view of the fjord below with aurora overhead. If aurora is not forecast, enjoy a relaxed evening at the hotel bar with Icelandic spirits.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon on rye bread, fresh juice
meals.lunch: Tasting from the morning cooking class — enjoy the dishes you prepared
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — request a lighter dinner after the cooking class lunch; opt for fresh fish of the day with seasonal vegetables

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class must be arranged in advance through the hotel concierge or local tourism contacts — expect to pay 15,000–25,000 ISK per person. This is an excellent opportunity to learn recipes to recreate at home. The aurora forecast should be checked by 18:00 to plan the evening — vedur.is provides hourly KP index predictions.

day_by_day.morning: Final Héðinsfjörður experience — return to the abandoned fjord for a longer, more contemplative winter hike. With familiarity from Day 2, venture deeper into the fjord toward the old farmstead ruins and the frozen waterfall at the fjord's head. The silence, the snow, and the towering basalt walls create a profound sense of wilderness solitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siglufjörður and visit the Herring Era Museum one final time to purchase premium souvenirs from the museum shop (books, prints, local crafts). Pack and prepare for tomorrow's departure. Enjoy a long, relaxing afternoon at the hotel — perhaps a final soak at the local swimming pool.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Hannes Boy — order your favourite dishes from the trip and ask the chef for a special dessert to mark the final evening. Afterward, take a final walk along the harbour under the stars, hoping for one last aurora display over the fjord.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full Icelandic spread; savour it as one of the last mornings
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka — final visit; order the fish soup and a slice of homemade cake
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy — farewell dinner; order the chef's recommendation and a bottle of fine wine to celebrate the journey

day_by_day.notes: Begin packing this evening to make tomorrow morning's departure smooth. Confirm your private transfer to Keflavík Airport for Day 13. Leave a review for Hotel Siglunes and Hannes Boy — small businesses in remote Icelandic towns depend on positive word-of-mouth. Check if any last-minute aurora activity is forecast for the night.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Siglufjörður — wake early for a last walk through the sleeping town in the pre-dawn darkness. Watch the slow winter sunrise (approximately 10:30–11:00 in January) paint the mountain peaks above the fjord in shades of pink and gold. Take final photographs of the harbour and town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Hotel Siglunes and begin the private luxury transfer south toward Keflavík. Stop in Akureyri for a final Icelandic lunch and any last-minute shopping (Icelandic wool sweaters, Brennivín, local chocolates, and books make excellent souvenirs). Continue south through the dramatic highland interior or coastal route depending on road conditions.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in the Reykjavík/Keflavík area by early evening. Check into a premium airport hotel (Hotel Keflavík, Icelandair Hotel Reykjavík Marina, or similar) for a comfortable final night. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at the hotel or a nearby Reykjavík restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast at Siglunes — take your time and enjoy every element
meals.lunch: Rub23 or Strikið Restaurant, Akureyri — a celebratory final Icelandic lunch with fresh seafood
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant near Keflavík or Reykjavík — Grillið at Radisson Blu Saga Hotel or Dill Restaurant (New Nordic cuisine, Michelin-starred) if time and reservation allow

day_by_day.notes: The transfer from Siglufjörður to Keflavík takes approximately 5–6 hours including stops — depart by 10:00 after checkout to arrive comfortably. Confirm road conditions (road.is) before departure, particularly for the highland routes in January. If Dill Restaurant is desired for the final dinner, reservations must be made weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland — if time allows before your departure flight, visit the famous Blue Lagoon geothermal spa (located just 20 minutes from Keflavík Airport). Book the premium Retreat Spa package for a final luxurious soak in the milky-blue silica-rich waters, complete with in-water massage, silica mud mask, and algae mask. A perfect, indulgent farewell to Iceland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Keflavík International Airport. Allow ample time for check-in and security. Browse the airport's duty-free for final Icelandic souvenirs: Icelandic wool products, Brennivín, Skyr snacks, and Icelandic sea salt. Board your Icelandair return flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Iceland — carry with you memories of the northern lights dancing over Siglufjörður's fjord, the warmth of geothermal pools against Arctic air, the silence of Héðinsfjörður, and the extraordinary privilege of experiencing one of the world's most remote and beautiful corners in the depths of winter.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast near Keflavík — light and early to allow time for Blue Lagoon visit
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon Lava Restaurant — premium in-spa dining with Icelandic seafood and New Nordic cuisine, enjoyed in your robe
meals.dinner: In-flight dining on Icelandair (upgrade to Saga Class for premium meal service if available)

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon must be booked well in advance — the Retreat Spa package (the most premium tier) costs approximately 60,000–80,000 ISK per person but includes exclusive access to the private lagoon, spa treatments, and restaurant dining. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before departure. Ensure all Icelandic currency is spent or exchanged — ISK cannot easily be converted outside Iceland. This concludes a truly extraordinary 13-day premium Iceland experience.
